biography: Josh Berry hails from the small town of Harmony, North Carolina, a place where racing isn't just a sport, it's a way of life. Unlike most drivers groomed from karting, Josh's entry into racing was almost accidental. He was helping his uncle fix up a beat-up late model stock car when, on a dare, he took it out for a spin on a local dirt track. The roar of the engine, the slide of the tires – it was an instant addiction. His inconsistent nature, however, led to frustrating moments. One week he'd be a contender, the next, crashing out in the first few laps. Despite these challenges, Josh caught the eye of the Stock USA Gen3 team after an unexpected podium finish at the Charlotte Motor Speedway. Currently, he's battling to prove he belongs in the Gen3 series, aiming to convert flashes of brilliance into consistent results and silence his doubters.
drivingStyle: Josh's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward approach. He's known for his aggressive entries into corners, often pushing the car right to the edge of grip. While this can lead to spectacular overtakes and impressive lap times, it also makes him prone to errors, especially when under pressure. He struggles with tire management, frequently burning through his rubber early in a stint, a consequence of his relentless pursuit of speed. He thrives in chaotic races, where his unpredictable nature can be an advantage, but consistency remains his biggest hurdle.

rivalries.reason: A clash at Daytona where Josh's aggressive move punted Alvarez into the wall, costing him the race.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky socks, no matter how worn out they are.

famousQuote: "You gotta risk it for the biscuit, even if the biscuit ends up stuck in the wall!"
careerHighlight: Winning the Charlotte Motor Speedway late model race in 2022 after starting from the back of the grid, showcasing his raw talent and determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out on the final lap of the Talladega race while leading, costing him his first Gen3 victory and a valuable points haul.
